changes.text: The software version and build are shown at the bottom left of the window, as on FortiOS. Click it to open the change log.
System > Change log lists every release with its build, date and changes.
The macOS app bundle and the PDF report carry the version and build.
The app has its own icon (firewall shield with an upgrade arrow) instead of the Python logo, for macOS (.icns) and Windows (.ico).

title: Per-unit HA addresses for service probes

changes.text: Default probes for an HA cluster target each unit's own management-ip or dedicated HA management interface, never the shared cluster address, so each unit's availability is shown separately.
A secondary's own address is read from the primary over SSH (execute ha manage, then show system interface) when it isn't saved on the device.
The HA cluster panel shows each unit's own address and fills it into Save addresses.

title: HA cluster view and upgrade hardening

changes.text: HA dashboard shows both units as appliances with the heartbeat link, role, HA priority, serial and cluster settings.
Save addresses re-saves a cluster as cluster address plus unit addresses, reusing its API token and SSH login.
The upgrade wizard adds probes for every management address automatically, respecting each interface's allowed access and the admin HTTPS port.
Temporary connection errors (TLS handshake refused, connection reset) on read-only API calls are retried twice instead of failing the upgrade.
An SSH login that stops at a password-change or disclaimer screen fails within seconds with a clear message, instead of hanging for 100 seconds.
HTTP(S) probes run at most once a second (default every 2 s), so they can't overload the FortiGate's management web server.

title: HA mode choice and dashboard layout

changes.text: A unit saved as Standalone that reports FGCP or FGSP is upgraded as a cluster, and the wizard asks for its HA upgrade and failover mode.
The wizard, device form and README explain the cluster address and per-unit HA management addresses.
Dashboard panels size to their content; text wraps instead of running past panel edges.
Rapid ping, TCP connect and HTTP(S) probes run during an upgrade and measure each outage window, tagged with the upgrade step that caused it.
Live timeline on the Install page, kept in the upgrade history and the PDF report.
The dashboard shows a FortiGate-VM's series (VM01, VM02, VM04 ... VMUL), licence type and vCPU/RAM allowance.

title: PDF report and FortiOS 8.0 backup fixes

changes.text: Server errors are logged and shown with their real message; the report retries from the saved job.
FortiOS 8.0's refusal of unencrypted backups is detected instead of being stored as configuration; the configuration is read over SSH instead.
The macOS build is swapped in atomically and warns when the app is running.
The wizard's final screen generates a PDF report: settings, pre-flight, per-device timeline, pre/post checks, diffs, warnings, errors and the activity log.
Local images are uploaded as a file (like the FortiOS GUI), avoiding HTTP 413; base64 is the fallback.
A failed upgrade shows the stage it failed in.
Device Configuration tab: view any saved configuration, diff two past configurations, or diff the current one against a chosen earlier one.
Firmware images are matched by model code, so FortiGate-VM and FortiFirewall images are recognised for the right devices.
Step-by-step upgrade wizard showing the target image and install method throughout, with Next buttons and warnings instead of typing UPGRADE.
Verbose live log in a terminal-style window, including every API and SSH call.
The dashboard draws each model's front panel with its physical ports only (no NPU links).
Secrets live in one encrypted vault with a single keychain item (or a local key file), ending repeated keychain prompts.
Per-device dashboard with tabs: system information, current status with compare, known issues, upgrade history and current jobs.
FortiOS-style look; the app is renamed FortiGate Upgrader.

Upgrades standalone FortiGates, FGCP and FGSP clusters over the REST API, with pre/post checks and diffs, upgrade path validation, FortiGuard download or local image push, HA upgrade modes, batch upgrades, a firmware store and FortiManager detection.
